original_value: Worst-case risk measures provide a means of calculating the largest value of risk when only partial information of the underlying distribution is available. For popular risk measures such as value-at-risk (VaR) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) it is now known that their worst-case counterparts can be evaluated in closed form when only the first two moments are known. We show in this paper that closed-form solutions exist for a general class of law invariant coherent risk measures, which consist of spectral risk measures (and thus CVaR also) as special cases. Moreover, we provide worst-case distributions characterized in terms of risk spectrums, which can take any form of distribution bounded from below. As applications of the closed-form results, new formulas are derived for calculating the worst-case values of higher order risk measures and higher order semideviation, and new robust portfolio optimization models are provided.  The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.2018.1736 .

result.paraphrase: Worst-case risk measures offer a way to compute the maximal risk value when only partial information about the underlying distribution is available. For widely used measures such as value-at-risk (VaR) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), it is now established that their worst-case versions admit closed-form evaluation when only the first two moments are known. In this paper, we show that closed-form solutions also exist for a broad class of law-invariant coherent risk measures, including spectral risk measures and therefore CVaR as a special case. We further describe worst-case distributions in terms of risk spectrums, which may have any distribution bounded below. Using these closed-form results, we derive new formulas for worst-case values of higher-order risk measures and higher-order semideviation, and we present new robust portfolio optimization models. The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.2018.1736 .
